title_en: Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Handling the Escape or Re-commission of Crimes by Reform-through-Labour Inmates and Persons under Re-education-through-Labour

articles.content_en: 1. With respect to the issue of whether the Decision shall apply to minors under the age of 16 who have been taken into custody by the government for education due to committing harmful acts and who commit crimes within three years after release from such education, this Court agrees with the opinion of your court, namely: Persons taken into custody by the government for education in accordance with Article 14, Paragraph 4 of the Criminal Law shall not be considered as reeducation-through-labor personnel; where they commit crimes again after release from education, the Decision shall not apply.

2. With respect to the issue of whether the Decision shall apply to offenders sentenced to criminal detention who commit crimes after escape or after release upon completion of the sentence, we are of the opinion that, in accordance with Articles 38 and 41 of the Criminal Law, offenders sentenced to criminal detention shall not be considered as reform-through-labor offenders. Therefore, where they commit crimes after escape or after release upon completion of the sentence, the Decision shall not apply.

3. With respect to the issue of whether the Decision shall apply to offenders sentenced to public surveillance or to fixed-term imprisonment with probation who commit crimes after expiration of public surveillance or after expiration of the probation period, this Court agrees with the opinion of your court, namely: Offenders sentenced to public surveillance or to fixed-term imprisonment with probation shall not be considered as reform-through-labor offenders. Therefore, where they commit crimes after expiration of public surveillance or after expiration of the probation period, the Decision shall not apply.
July 24, 1993
